dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e📂 Automatic State Persistence\u003c/strong\u003e\nEvery action (files created, commands run, features completed) is saved to a hidden \u003ccode\u003e.vebgen/\u003c/code\u003e folder in your project. Close VebGen mid-development? The AI picks up exactly where it stopped—with full memory of what's been built, what's pending, and what failed.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/blockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e📖 \u003cstrong\u003eState Management Details\u003c/strong\u003e: See \u003ca href=\"/vebgenofficial/vebgen/blob/main/docs/memory_manager.md\"\u003eMemory Manager Documentation\u003c/a\u003e for backup algorithms and \u003ca href=\"/vebgenofficial/vebgen/blob/main/docs/project_models.md\"\u003eProject Models Documentation\u003c/a\u003e for state schema.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e🔐 Corruption Protection with SHA-256 Verification\u003c/strong\u003e\u003cbr\u003e\nEvery time VebGen saves your project state, it calculates a \u003cstrong\u003eSHA-256 cryptographic hash\u003c/strong\u003e of the data. When loading, it verifies the hash matches—if it doesn't (file corruption, system crash, disk error), VebGen \u003cstrong\u003eautomatically restores from the most recent valid backup\u003c/strong\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e🗂️ 5 Automatic Backups (Timestamped)\u003c/strong\u003e\u003cbr\u003e\nBefore saving any state changes, VebGen creates a timestamped backup. It keeps the \u003cstrong\u003e5 most recent backups\u003c/strong\u003e, pruning older ones automatically. If all 5 backups are tested during recovery and fail, VebGen notifies you instead of silently using corrupted data.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e⚡ Atomic Writes Prevent Partial Saves\u003c/strong\u003e\u003cbr\u003e\nState files are written to a temporary file first, then atomically swapped using \u003ccode\u003eos.replace()\u003c/code\u003e. This means if the system crashes mid-save (power loss, force quit), the old file remains intact—\u003cstrong\u003eno partial writes, no corrupted state\u003c/strong\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e🔒 Thread-Safe Operations\u003c/strong\u003e\u003cbr\u003e\nAll file operations use a \u003ccode\u003ethreading.Lock\u003c/code\u003e to prevent race conditions. Multiple parts of VebGen can request saves simultaneously without data corruption.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e🗑️ Soft-Delete Trash System\u003c/strong\u003e\u003cbr\u003e\nWhen state files are \"deleted,\" they're actually moved to \u003ccode\u003e.vebgen/trash/\u003c/code\u003e with timestamps. Every file modification is validated before being committed. If \u003ccode\u003eCASE\u003c/code\u003e introduces a syntax error, VebGen \u003cstrong\u003einstantly reverts the change\u003c/strong\u003e and tries a different approach.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003c/blockquote\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e📸 Snapshot-Based Rollback System\u003c/strong\u003e\u003cbr\u003e\nBefore every risky operation (file writes, patches, command execution), VebGen creates a \u003cstrong\u003elightweight snapshot\u003c/strong\u003e of affected files. If anything fails, the entire operation rolls back atomically—\u003cstrong\u003eno partial changes, no corrupted state\u003c/strong\u003e.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eRollback triggers include:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eSyntax errors after patching\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eFailed patch application (context mismatch)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eCommand execution failures\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003eUser-initiated abort (ROLLBACK action)\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ul\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e🔁 3-Attempt Remediation Loop\u003c/strong\u003e\u003cbr\u003e\nWhen \u003ccode\u003eCASE\u003c/code\u003e fails a feature, \u003ccode\u003eTARS\u003c/code\u003e doesn't just give up. Here's what actually happens:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003col dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eFirst attempt fails\u003c/strong\u003e → TARS reviews the work, identifies mistakes\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eSecond attempt\u003c/strong\u003e with correction instructions from TARS\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eThird attempt\u003c/strong\u003e with stricter guidance if still failing\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eAfter 3 failures\u003c/strong\u003e → System escalates with detailed error report\u003c/li\u003e\n\u003c/ol\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003eEach retry gets \u003cstrong\u003esmarter\u003c/strong\u003e because TARS provides increasingly specific correction instructions based on the failure history.\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cp dir=\"auto\"\u003e\u003cstrong\u003e🚦 Circuit Breaker (Anti-Loop Protection)\u003c/strong\u003e\u003cbr\u003e\nVebGen detects \u003cstrong\u003erepetitive action patterns\u003c/strong\u003e that indicate the agent is stuck:\u003c/p\u003e\n\u003cul dir=\"auto\"\u003e\n\u003cli\u003e\u003cstrong\u003eA→B→A
